side.notes: Sources agree on the deep disc/diamond body, concave forehead, terminal mouth, tall triangular median fins, truncate tail, elongated pelvic rays, and four-bar adult pattern.

top.uncertainty: High. No verified true orthographic whole-fish top photograph was found; half-width stations only implement FishBase's highly compressed classification.
top.notes: Top width is intentionally conservative and must remain visually reviewable rather than treated as measured.

front.uncertainty: High. No verified true orthographic frontal photograph was found; head width, eye seating, and terminal lip volume are inferred from compressed-body classification and lateral imagery.
front.notes: The front profile cannot be accepted as source-measured until a verified frontal original is added.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: highly compressed disc/diamond trunk and concave dorsal head
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Deep anal-level stations, narrow half-widths, and a forehead saddle before the terminal snout prevent a generic oval cichlid or marine-angelfish profile.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: tall triangular dorsal and anal envelopes with long first branched rays
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Posterior-increasing spines lead into the tallest early soft rays, then taper to the peduncle, forming the characteristic upper and lower triangles.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: truncate caudal streamers and elongated thoracic pelvic rays
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: A shallow central caudal cut leaves longer dorsal and ventral edges, while narrow paired pelvic sheets and distal filaments extend from the thorax.

proportions.name: maximum adult total length
proportions.notes: The 84 mm station-defined standard length plus the 21 mm caudal envelope targets FishBase's 10.5 cm total length.

proportions.name: standard length divided by body height at anal level
proportions.notes: The source evaluates to 0.084 / (0.037 + 0.035) = 1.167, inside FishBase's 1.07 to 1.29 range.

proportions.name: maximum width divided by anal-level body height
proportions.uncertainty: High. FishBase establishes compression but does not provide a calibrated width, and no true top or frontal original was found.
proportions.notes: The narrow source guards against a balloon body while keeping the exact width explicitly provisional.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: adult four-bar silver pattern
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Four procedural dark bars cross the eye, shoulder, midbody, and caudal base; the seven-bar juvenile pattern is explicitly excluded.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: silver-olive body and translucent ray-supported fins
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Silver flank sheen, restrained olive dorsum, pale belly, and translucent fins are generated procedurally with fixed seeds.

mismatches.note: Reject any candidate that reads as a generic oval cichlid, tang, or balloon. The side view must preserve the narrow disc/diamond trunk, forehead saddle, tiny terminal mouth, narrow peduncle, tall median-fin triangles, and long pelvic threads.
Reject seven juvenile bars, decorative striping, or a uniform silver body. The baseline is an adult four-bar wild-type pattern.
Do not promote a candidate merely because the side view is recognizable. Top width and frontal head volume remain high-uncertainty inferences requiring downstream visual review.

uncertainty: True top and frontal views are unavailable. Backend geometry can represent the sourced side silhouette, measured depth ratio, fins, terminal mouth, and four-bar adult pattern, but a built candidate still requires explicit visual acceptance.
pixelPolicy: No reference pixels are copied, sampled, traced, redistributed, embedded, or hotlinked.
